subject: Exclusion matrix + sample language for direct vs indirect damages (MSA / Order Form)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Boyd <sarah.boyd@acme-tech.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme-tech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Exclusion matrix + sample language for direct vs indirect damages (MSA / Order Form)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is our initial pass: MSA + Order Form redlines (v1) and a lightweight "exclusion matrix" that maps the common loss categories (lost profits, loss of data, loss of goodwill) to proposed carve-outs and sample wording.

High-level approach we think will keep procurement happy while protecting both parties:
- Base cap: fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months prior to the claim.
- Direct damages: allow remediation costs and reasonable restoration costs (e.g., data recovery, customer notification) as recoverable.
- Excluded indirect damages: lost profits, loss of goodwill, and consequential business interruption are excluded as a default.
- Exception carve-outs: deliberate data destruction or unauthorized exfiltration where Redwood is grossly negligent or commits willful misconduct -> limited carve-out for lost profits (narrowly defined).

Two sample snippets included in the PDF: Option A (narrow carve-out — remediation only) and Option B (broader but capped at 2x fees with high audit/forensics standards). Please review with your legal folks; we kept the language conservative to avoid reopening the entire MSA.

Ask: Can you flag which parts of the matrix you want tracked as "non-starters" vs "needs more review"? If you prefer, we can offer a side-by-side redline with their suggested language.

Attachments: MSA_OrderForm_redlines_v1.pdf (redlines + sample snippets), exclusion_matrix.xlsx (mapping table)

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Exclusion matrix + sample language for direct vs indirect damages (MSA / Order Form)

Kimberly —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the matrix; that format is helpful. A few immediate notes from Acme legal/procurement:

1) We cannot accept an open carve-out for lost profits tied to gross negligence. Our legal team needs a very high bar (e.g., willful misconduct or intentional wrongdoing) to permit recovery of lost profits.
2) We are generally okay with remediation costs (data restoration, reasonable customer notification costs) being recoverable as direct damages, provided there are corroborating forensics and a cap tied to fees.
3) For loss of goodwill, we will push to keep that excluded.
4) We will ask for SOC 2 Type II and an encryption attestation before signing; please point us to those docs.

Can you propose alternate language that replaces "gross negligence" with "willful misconduct" in the lost-profits exception, and make the scope of recoverable remediation costs explicit (time/labor/materials/forensics only)? Also, is Redwood willing to accept a mutual cap (both sides limited to the same fee-based formula)?

Sarah
Sarah Boyd
Head of Legal Ops, Acme Tech
sarah.boyd@acme-tech.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exclusion matrix + sample language for direct vs indirect damages (MSA / Order Form)

Kimberly / team —

Saw Sarah's notes. I revised the matrix and drafted an alternate snippet that:
- Replaces "gross negligence" with "willful misconduct" where Acme asked, but narrows what "lost profits" means (third-party contract breach / demonstrable incremental revenue only).
- Clarifies recoverable remediation costs to: (a) reasonable data restoration costs; (b) forensic investigation fees; (c) customer notification and credit-monitoring only if required by law.
- Offers two caps: (i) mutual cap = fees paid in prior 12 months; (ii) mutual cap = 2x fees if willful misconduct is established and subject to indemnity-specific procedures.

Proposed inline redline (suggested merge into Section 9 Limitations):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party shall be liable to the other for indirect, special, punitive, incidental, or consequential damages, including lost profits, loss of business, or loss of goodwill, except that (i) either party may recover direct damages for reasonable remediation costs, and (ii) in cases of proven willful misconduct resulting in demonstrable third-party lost profits, recovery shall be limited to the lesser of actual lost profits and two times the fees paid under the applicable Order Form in the prior twelve (12) months."

I attached an updated exclusion_matrix.xlsx with column 'Acme ask' and our recommended text.

Thoughts? If Acme pushes to keep "gross negligence" then we can ask for a "procedural gate" (forensics first, independent investigator) as an alternative.

-Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Exclusion matrix + sample language for direct vs indirect damages (MSA / Order Form)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for the quick feedback and the SOC 2 note. We can provide SOC 2 Type II and an encryption attestation; I will attach the certs to a secure share once I hear back from you on the language below.

Inline redline (short):
"Direct damages" means actual, direct, and provable damages incurred by the non-breaching party (including reasonable and documented costs of: (i) data restoration; (ii) forensics; and (iii) legally required customer notifications).
"Excluded damages" expressly include lost profits, loss of goodwill, and other consequential losses, except to the extent such losses arise from proven willful misconduct as defined in this Agreement. Where willful misconduct is alleged, the claiming party must (a) provide a prima facie showing to trigger entitlement to discovery; and (b) permit an independent forensic review to validate quantum and causation prior to recovery.

We are also willing to make the cap mutual (same formula for both parties) if Acme accepts the independent-forensics procedural gate and a 2x-fees cap in the willful-misconduct path.

Can you confirm your legal team's preference on: (1) "willful misconduct" vs "gross negligence"; (2) whether a mutual cap is acceptable; and (3) whether Acme will accept the independent-forensics step? We'd like to close this week if possible.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Jasmine / Kimberly —

Thanks — this is mostly inline with what our GC is willing to accept. A couple of follow-ups:

- Our GC prefers the term "willful misconduct" (good).
- We are comfortable with a mutual cap so long as the independent-forensics step is spelled out (who selects the vendor, timelines, and cost-shifting if the claim is unfounded). Please add language that (i) the parties will jointly select an independent forensic vendor within 10 business days; (ii) costs are borne by the losing party; and (iii) we have a 90-day remediation window prior to submitting a claim for lost profits.
- We cannot share recent customer order forms. If you can provide anonymized examples or a redacted bundle, that would help our procurement team.

Assuming you accept the forensics/timelines language, procurement will sign off and route to our GC for final counters.

Best,
Sarah
